policy: Only binary relations are admitted. Any pair not confidently resolvable is excluded rather than labeled ambiguous.

pairs.adjudicationRationale: A cross-group terminal-state scope failure and storage-round-trip key-order sensitivity occur in different state-machine and persistence boundaries; changing either boundary does not address the other.
Case-sensitive grouping changes recurrence identity, while an unreachable truncation threshold changes output handling; one coherent correction would not address both.
A constant response passing through an oversized truncation guard concerns output bounds; deriving current-head state from an event commit concerns state context. They are independent.

Both are independently observable consequences of flattening a list of abstraction descriptions into comma-joined display text: the representation is unbounded and is ambiguous when values contain commas.
Counting an ancestor commit as a later recurrence concerns event chronology; unused exports concern module surface. They require unrelated changes.
Reusing a prior review identifier as a correction identifier concerns identifier validity; ambiguous comma-joined display text concerns list encoding.
Both are restore-time consequences of replaying historical events under a failing restore path: one causes restoration failure and the other makes read-only status unavailable after that failure.

Both arise because occurrence aggregation and correction recording use inconsistent identity boundaries: one correction leaves a same-category record open, and one correction commit can be counted twice.
Duplicate correction counting concerns identity scope; quadratic event copying concerns append complexity. Neither correction addresses the other.
Historical validation incompatibility concerns persistence replay; unused exports concern module surface.
Quadratic append copying is a history-size cost; naming an earlier unresolved observation stale is a finding-state presentation error.
An unreachable prior-occurrence branch concerns reducer control flow; event-commit head derivation concerns assessment context.
Reporting only the first qualifying group concerns multi-group result completeness; computing unused head partitions concerns unnecessary state derivation.
Read-only status failing after restore error concerns failure containment; accepting a prior review identifier as a correction identifier concerns identifier validity.
Requiring separate corrections for descriptions aggregated as one category concerns identity consistency; labeling older unresolved observations stale concerns state terminology.
An observation remaining in recurrence counts after contradiction concerns lifecycle withdrawal; unbounded abstraction display concatenation concerns output representation.

adequacy.purpose: Bounded feasibility corpus, not a prevalence or tolerance estimator.
adequacy.constraint: A later classification protocol must preregister attainable exact-count criteria and uncertainty. Run 2 percentage thresholds are not inherited. Expanding or relabeling this gold set requires a new corpus-validation run.
